about.title: About this breakdown
about.region_FAO: Region here means FAO major fishing area, not Indian state — Area 51 is the Arabian Sea (west) coast, Area 57 the Bay of Bengal (east) coast and Andaman & Nicobar. FAO does not report a state-level split (Kerala / Goa / Odisha).
about.region_SAU: Region here means EEZ, not Indian state — Sea Around Us reports catch by exclusive economic zone, so a state-level split (Kerala / Goa / Odisha) is not derivable from this source.
about.grouping: Grouping by species charts the eight largest by total catch; the remainder are summed into "Other" so the yearly totals still add up.
about.measure_FAO: These are officially reported landings (FAO Global Capture Production, CC BY 4.0). They exclude discards and unreported catch, so they run well below the Sea Around Us reconstruction — the two are different measurements and must not be compared year-for-year or summed. Some species only appear once India began reporting them separately (e.g. black pomfret from 2019).
about.measure_SAU: These are reconstructed figures including estimated discards and unreported catch. They are not comparable with the FAO reported-landings series and must not be summed with it.

molecular.subtitleSuffix: This is the reference library you match unknown sequences against.

about.title: What is this section, and is it eDNA?
about.barcode: A DNA barcode is a short, standardised stretch of an organism's DNA that acts like a fingerprint for its species. Most records here use COI-5P, the standard marker for animals; the rest use 16S, rbcL and a few others.
about.notEdna: Strictly, this is not eDNA. Environmental DNA means genetic traces recovered from a water sample, letting you detect species without catching them. These records come from physical specimens that were collected and sequenced. They are the reference library an eDNA study would compare its water samples against — necessary for eDNA work, but not eDNA results themselves. Actual water-sample detections would need a separate data source and are not in this platform.
about.columns: What each column means. Process ID is BOLD's identifier for the record. Identification is the species the specimen was assigned to. Marker is which gene region was sequenced. BIN is BOLD's own cluster of near-identical barcodes, roughly a species-level grouping — useful when two records agree genetically but were named differently.
about.whatYouCanDo: What you can do here. Paste a sequence into the search above and it will be ranked against all {{total}} records by composition similarity, returning the most likely species matches.

search.title: Barcode similarity search
search.placeholder: Paste a nucleotide sequence (FASTA headers, gaps and ambiguity codes are stripped automatically)…

result.caveat: Composition-based ranking, not sequence alignment. It cannot detect insertions/deletions or report an E-value, and two sequences sharing composition in a different order will score as near-identical. Use BLAST or the BOLD ID Engine for an authoritative identification.

plain.title: In plain words, what this result means
plain.closest: The closest match found is , at {{pct}}% similarity.
plain.bandStrong: That is a very close match — this sample most likely belongs to that species.
plain.bandFair: That is a fairly close match — probably that species or a close relative, but not certain enough to say for sure.
plain.bandWeak: That isn't a strong match to anything in the library — treat this result as inconclusive.
plain.similarityMeans: "Similarity" here means how alike the short repeating DNA patterns are between your sequence and each library record — like comparing two pieces of text for how many 5-letter chunks they share, not reading and matching every single letter in order.
plain.checkedAgainst: Your sequence was checked against {{count}} real DNA records in the library, and the table above shows the closest ones found, best match first.
plain.estimate: This is a quick estimate, not a lab-certified identification — it can be fooled by sequences that share a similar pattern but aren't actually related. For a confirmed identification, the result would need checking with proper alignment tools (like BLAST).
plain.noMatch: No record in the library shared any DNA pattern with this sequence — it may belong to a species that simply isn't in this reference library yet.

correlation.subtitleSuffix: Satellite and weather series resampled to monthly values and joined on month.

plain.title: What this means in plain words
plain.positive: {{x}} and {{y}} tend to rise together — as {{x}} goes up, {{y}} tends to go up too.
plain.negative: {{x}} and {{y}} move in opposite directions — as {{x}} goes up, {{y}} tends to go down.
plain.strength: That's {{strength}} (correlation of {{r}}, where 0 means no relationship at all and ±1 would mean they move perfectly together).
plain.significant_one: This pattern is statistically significant (p = {{p}}) — unlikely to just be random noise, given {{count}} month of data.
plain.significant_other: This pattern is statistically significant (p = {{p}}) — unlikely to just be random noise, given {{count}} months of data.
plain.notSignificant_one: This pattern is not statistically significant — with only {{count}} month of overlapping data, it could plausibly just be random noise rather than a real relationship.
plain.notSignificant_other: This pattern is not statistically significant — with only {{count}} months of overlapping data, it could plausibly just be random noise rather than a real relationship.
plain.causation: Correlation isn't causation — this says the two move together, not that one causes the other. Both could be driven by something else entirely (like the seasons).

notes.region_ignored: Region filters do not apply to satellite variables: grid cells sit in open ocean and carry no region, so those series remain national.
notes.too_few_months_one: Only {{count}} overlapping month — too few to correlate.
notes.too_few_months_other: Only {{count}} overlapping months — too few to correlate.
notes.indicative_one: Based on {{count}} monthly point; treat the coefficient as indicative, not conclusive.
notes.indicative_other: Based on {{count}} monthly points; treat the coefficient as indicative, not conclusive.
notes.spatial_means: Computed on spatial averages across stations — this describes national month-to-month co-movement, not a relationship at any single location.
notes.chlorophyll_median: Chlorophyll uses the monthly median, not the mean: its values are heavily skewed, and a mean would follow a few turbid coastal cells rather than the whole basin.
